 Spotlight
 

Next mobility quest

What’s happening? Dubai’s Roads and Transport Authority has opened registration for the 14th Dubai Awards for Sustainable Transport 2026 (DAST 2026). The award invites government bodies, private companies, schools, researchers, transport experts, and students to submit projects, research, or ideas that can improve sustainable mobility. Launched in 2008, DAST rewards innovation in clean, safe, inclusive, and environmentally friendly transport.

Categories: DAST 2026 includes four main categories. Sustainability focuses on green and environmentally friendly transport solutions. Innovation rewards fresh mobility ideas, including student and next-generation projects. Inclusivity recognises safe, accessible, and transport-for-all initiatives. Elite honours the strongest idea, project, or research concept chosen from across all categories by the jury, making it the award’s top recognition.

How to apply? Applicants can register for DAST 2026 through the RTA’s official DAST digital portal. They must first create an account by registering their organisation, whether government, private, or educational, or sign in as an individual researcher. Next, they should choose the award category that best matches their project. Once all details are complete, they can submit the application before the June 2026 deadline.
 
 

What your credit report may be hiding

 

Credit check: Your credit score does not always tell the full story. Errors, outdated information, or negative marks on your credit report can quietly affect borrowing costs, approvals, and financial options without you fully realizing it.

Why it matters: Lexington Law offers a free credit assessment designed to help people understand what may be affecting their credit. The idea is simple. Before making any big financial move, it helps to know what is actually on your report and what could be holding you back.

What you get: For readers who want a clearer picture of their credit without jumping straight into a commitment, this is an easy first step. The positioning is practical and low-friction, with the added credibility of coming from a law firm rather than just another credit tool.

Where to eat?
 

Yubi Handroll Bar introduces a refined dining experience at 25 Jump Street in One Central. Created by 7 Management in collaboration with chef Reif Othman, the menu blends Japanese street-food tradition with a hip-hop vibe. The interior features a long bar where diners sit on stools and watch chefs prepare hand-rolls on demand. The design mixes natural wood, soft lighting, textured wall murals, and neon accents, creating a lively blend of street style and elegance.

Pro tip: Sit at the counter for a front-row view of the hand-roll craft and ask the chef for the “chef’s roll.”

Meanwhile
 

Parking gets smarter

Parkin has started installing AI-enabled cameras across busy areas to automate parking fee collection and monitor parking spaces in real time. The first phase includes more than 500 curb- and pole-mounted cameras in areas such as Burj Khalifa, Trade Centre 1, and Al Corniche, along with 200 more cameras in controlled parking lots. The solar-powered system reads number plates, records entry and exit times, tracks parking duration, and enables automatic payment through the Parkin app and digital wallet.

Fees made flexible

UAE schools are providing flexible payment plans to help families manage rising education expenses and monetary pressure. Several schools are working directly with parents to create tailored fee arrangements, including monthly instalments, deferred payments, sibling discounts, scholarships, and customised support. The focus is on easing short-term pressure, keeping education accessible, and ensuring students continue learning without disruption.

Banking seat bid

The UAE is seeking a seat on the board of Swift, the global messaging network used by banks and monetary institutions for cross-border payments. UAE Banks Federation officials said discussions are underway as the country rises in global rankings for trade-related payment activity. A board seat would give the UAE greater visibility in global payments infrastructure, banking standards, cybersecurity, and cross-border systems.
